Bek Lover joins Danny Jones for a bold talk that calls Jeffrey Epstein God's final messenger. The title also links the claim to Jesus, jihad, and Bible prophecy. Lover brings a street level, faith charged style to the mic.

Lover lays out his view of Epstein as a sign in a larger holy plan. The talk swings from scripture to war in the Middle East and back. Jones lets the guest run, then tests the logic of the claim. The episode is raw and sure to split its audience. The library keeps it as an archive record of the guest's stated beliefs.
podcast-joerogan-dKvFLwFSnlw:
Could sound waves have built the Great Pyramids? Rogan chews on that wild theory in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. The claim is that tones and vibration moved the great stones, a piece of fringe archaeology built on legends of priests who sang rocks into place.

The talk tests the idea against what is known of Egyptian building, and enjoys the gap between the two. Rogan asks what proof could ever exist for such a method. The segment is the show at play: a dreamy theory, taken seriously for an hour, by a host who loves the question more than any answer.
